PullRequest.Title: agentHost: avoid redundant changeset operation refreshes
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Fixes an Agent Host performance regression where a session workspace change could refresh every chat and folder changeset owner, repeatedly publishing unchanged operation state.

- narrow session folder invalidation to chats that inherit the session folders
- coalesce overlapping session, GitHub, and pull request operation refreshes
- skip `changeset/operationsChanged` actions when the computed operations are unchanged
- retain branch summaries shared by multiple chats
- cover `set_workspace` and `create_session` with `relationship: currentSession` in a 32-chat, 804-subscription session

## Testing

- `npm run transpile-client` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostChangesetOperationService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostChangesetCoordinator.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostChangesetService.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostContributions.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostChangesetStrategy.test.ts` — passed, 321 tests
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostChangesetOperationService.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostChangesetCoordinator.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostChangesetOperationService.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostChangesetCoordinator.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostChangesetOperationService.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostChangesetService.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostContributions.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostChangesetStrategy.test.ts` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — blocked by unrelated existing Copilot SDK typing, missing `libsodium-wrappers`, and local transcription errors; no errors were reported in the changed files

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A session-level refresh synchronously recomputed and published an operations action for every subscribed changeset even when all computed operation arrays were unchanged, multiplying state-envelope and downstream serialization/consumer work by subscription count.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Workspace/configuration and operation-provider events in a 32-chat session with 804 subscriptions could publish hundreds of redundant unchanged operation envelopes, causing avoidable CPU/IPC fan-out and latency.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The new helper compares the computed operation list with the changeset's current operations and returns before dispatching an unchanged action; event-triggered refresh requests are also coalesced per microtask and owner, bounding duplicate computations within one burst.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 274 unconditionally dispatches ChangesetOperationsChanged after every operation recomputation. updateOperations(session) expands through _getOperationOwners to each chat/folder owner and then every subscribed changeset. The added large-session test establishes a realistic 32-chat/804-subscription workspace-change scenario and asserts that unchanged operation state previously reached this publication path; the new _dispatchOperationsChanged equality guard suppresses those unchanged actions. Blame identifies the unconditional publication as introduced by fe9f87ca05dca0086aabaf24c7ffaf33888e2a1d.

Scenarios.Scenario: Session workspace changes, including set_workspace and create_session relationship=currentSession, in a multi-chat session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The working-directory state event synchronously updates monitor/recompute bookkeeping and schedules one operation-update microtask. Git-state refreshes, repository-root resolution, diff work, and watcher attachment are fire-and-forget/queued and are not awaited by the workspace-change handler; the operation microtask runs before the next macrotask. Warm unchanged operations no longer reach protocol broadcast.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Broadcast a ChangesetOperationsChanged state envelope to connected clients.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For the realistic test fixture of 32 chats and 804 subscriptions, operation computation can still visit the effective subscribed changesets once per deduplicated owner, but warm unchanged state emits 0 envelopes; cold/changed state emits at most one envelope per changed subscribed changeset.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each recomputed subscription unconditionally emitted an envelope, yielding up to 804 redundant publications in the supplied large-session scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Envelope emission is synchronous with the microtask flush and downstream serialization/broadcast; the equality guard removes this work entirely for unchanged results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query Git state for an affected chat working directory through IAgentHostGitService.getSessionGitState.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One refresh per chat whose working directories inherit from the changed session; explicitly scoped chats are now excluded. Calls are throttled per key, while distinct chat keys can run concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The coordinator refreshed every chat after a session working-directory change, including explicitly scoped chats; the diff narrows this to inheriting chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Invoked without awaiting from the coordinator, so it is off the immediate event-handler critical path but can create background Git load.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve repository roots and reattach shared file watchers when the effective directory signature changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coordinator notification for the session plus one per inheriting chat/subagent; each resolution groups duplicate repository roots and limits working-directory lookups within a request. Unchanged signatures are warm no-ops.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The session and every chat were notified; the diff retains the session notification and excludes chats with explicit working directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queued through per-key sequencers and not awaited by the workspace event handler.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Schedule branch/session/turn/uncommitted diff recomputations, including worker and Git/filesystem work in downstream implementations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for the session when applicable and once per inheriting chat, with static recomputes coalesced by owner/kind; explicitly scoped chats no longer participate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Recomputation was requested for every chat regardless of whether it inherited the session folders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dispatch over subscriptions is synchronous, but heavy recomputations are scheduled/async.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective owner and subscription counts after Set-based coalescing; the PR's realistic fixture establishes 32 chats and 804 subscribed changesets. Background Git/file work scales only with chats inheriting session folders after the change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Operation recomputation is synchronous and serialized in one microtask with owner deduplication. Git refresh uses per-key throttlers, so distinct affected chats may run concurrently. Watch attachment is sequenced per owner, and repository-root lookups are limited within each resolution request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Operation results are read from changeset state and compared structurally; warm unchanged results suppress publication, while changed/cold results publish once. File-monitor attachment uses working-directory signatures and shared root acquisitions; operation refresh requests are coalesced within one microtask.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed call paths, 32-chat/804-subscription test, equality guard, and per-key scheduling are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual Git duration and the number of inheriting versus explicitly scoped chats vary by session, but the diff reduces those boundary calls and removes unchanged IPC envelopes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff coalesces duplicate operation work, suppresses unchanged IPC fan-out, and narrows filesystem/Git work to chats actually affected by the session folder change.

Scenarios.Scenario: GitHub, pull-request status, and operation-provider events refreshing advertised changeset operations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The event adds a resource key to a Set and schedules one microtask; the flush expands related owners, computes operations from in-memory state, deduplicates owner overlap, and broadcasts only changed arrays. No GitHub/network request is initiated by the new scheduling path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish changed advertised-operation arrays to clients.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one computation per effective owner per microtask burst and one envelope per changeset whose operation array actually differs; repeated same-key events in the burst collapse to one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every provider event immediately expanded related owners and unconditionally republished every subscribed changeset, including unchanged arrays.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in the scheduled microtask; unchanged warm state performs no broadcast.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostGitStateService.ts pull-request lookup paths upstream of onDidChangeSessionGitHubState
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve pull-request/GitHub state before emitting the state-change event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Serialized per session/folder key by the existing pull-request sequencer; this diff adds no lookup and only consumes the resulting event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same upstream lookup/event existed, followed by immediate unconditional operation publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The network request precedes the event but is not added or moved by this diff; operation recomputation follows from cached state.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct event resource keys, effective related owners after Set deduplication, and subscribed changesets per owner.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous flush processes the burst; there is no async fan-out in operation computation. Upstream network lookups remain serialized per key by existing sequencers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Git/GitHub state is read from existing state-manager/service caches. Same-key requests coalesce within a microtask, and unchanged operation arrays act as a positive equality cache for publication. There is no new negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all production callers and the 196,000-call burst test show Set/microtask coalescing to one effective computation for one owner.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency and burst shape of production provider events vary, but all changed mechanisms bound rather than amplify work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed scheduling reduces repeated computation and IPC fan-out without introducing a boundary call.

Scenarios.Scenario: Shared branch-summary setup, reconciliation, chat removal, config transition, and session disposal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Reconciliation records one source entry per chat so shared branch resources survive removal of one source. Branch refresh and watcher tracking are invoked during setup; monitor acquisition and diff computation are queued. Removal checks remaining references before untracking, and session disposal clears the source map before idempotent cleanup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire or release shared repository-root file watcher interest for a branch changeset resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: trackSessionChanges is keyed by the branch changeset URI, so multiple chats sharing one resource create one watch-interest reference; removal retains it while another source refers to the resource and releases it after the last reference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Tracking was already called for each desired source but the resource-keyed map could lose source ownership and release a shared resource when one chat disappeared; the diff retains source ownership without multiplying watcher acquisitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Map/reference bookkeeping is synchronous; repository-root resolution and watcher acquisition are queued asynchronously. Warm repeated tracking of the same subscription key is a no-op.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Schedule branch diff computation backed by Git/filesystem work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Reconciliation still invokes refresh per desired source as before; downstream static recompute scheduling coalesces by owner/kind. The source-keyed map does not add a new refresh boundary on the normal setup path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-source reconciliation loop called _ensureBranchSummarySubscription and refreshBranchChangeset before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Scheduling is synchronous but heavy compute is deferred.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chats/sources and number of unique branch resources after scope resolution. A tested case has multiple chats sharing one repository resource; the large-session fixture has 32 chats.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Source reconciliation is synchronous. Watch attachment and static recomputation use existing per-key sequencing/coalescing; no new aggregate concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Watcher interest is keyed by resource and shared across source entries. Branch recomputation uses existing scheduled-static-recompute coalescing. The new source map retains O(chat count) small ownership records for session lifetime, then clears them on removal/disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for source/resource accounting and watcher deduplication; repository code directly shows keyed DisposableMap and scheduled recompute behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The rare summary-kind transition can revisit a shared resource once per source for in-memory operation computation, but operation arrays are small and publication is equality-suppressed; this does not establish user-visible degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra per-source bookkeeping is bounded by existing chat state and prevents premature shared-resource cleanup; expensive watcher/diff boundaries remain keyed and coalesced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and all diff pages. The PR removes a validated 804-subscription unchanged-action fan-out regression (recorded separately with its blamed introducer), narrows workspace invalidation, and preserves shared watcher ownership. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
